questions.q: Examine the main causes of the Revolt of 1857.
answer: The Revolt of 1857 grew out of many grievances that had built up under Company rule.

answer.text: Annexations under the Doctrine of Lapse, such as Jhansi and Satara, the annexation of Awadh in 1856, and the ending of pensions like that of Nana Saheb, angered rulers and nobles.
Heavy taxes ruined peasants and artisans, while interference in customs and the fear that the British wished to convert Indians to Christianity alarmed both Hindus and Muslims.
Sepoys were discontented over pay and prospects, and the immediate spark was the new greased cartridges, rumoured to be coated with cow and pig fat, which offended the religion of both communities.

questions.q: Describe the outbreak of the Revolt of 1857 and its consequences.

answer.text: Mangal Pandey fired the first shots at Barrackpore, and the revolt proper began at Meerut on 10 May 1857. The rebels marched to Delhi and proclaimed the aged Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar their leader. It spread across north and central India, led by Nana Saheb and Tantia Tope at Kanpur, Rani Lakshmibai at Jhansi, Begum Hazrat Mahal at Lucknow and Kunwar Singh in Bihar.

The British crushed the revolt by 1858 and exiled Bahadur Shah Zafar to Rangoon. By the Government of India Act of 1858, the East India Company's rule ended and India came under the direct rule of the British Crown. Queen Victoria's Proclamation promised no further annexations and respect for religion, and the Governor-General became the Viceroy.
